name: Cherenkov timing in PET
summary: Prompt Cherenkov photons from 511 keV photoelectrons in dense crystals such as BGO are being exploited as a fast timing signal toward sub-100 ps time-of-flight PET.

name: Liénard–Wiechert to undulator radiation
summary: Bending-magnet and undulator spectra, critical energy and relativistic beaming follow from Liénard–Wiechert/Larmor radiation with γ-boosted forward cones; coherent emission scales as N² when bunches are shorter than the wavelength.

name: Compton and Rayleigh scattering in X-ray imaging
summary: X-ray attenuation in imaging combines photoelectric absorption (∝Z³/E³, the main contrast source), Compton scattering (dominant in soft tissue above ~30 keV, Klein–Nishina) and Rayleigh scattering. Scattered photons degrade radiograph and CT contrast, so anti-scatter grids and corrections are used.

name: H-theorem: a dynamical second law
summary: Boltzmann's H-function is minus the entropy, and the Stosszahlansatz makes dH/dt≤0. Loschmidt's reversibility paradox and Zermelo's recurrence paradox show that the arrow of time comes from the low-entropy initial condition and from coarse-graining.

name: Liquid–gas critical point in the 3D Ising class
summary: The end point of the liquid–vapour line, where the Clausius–Clapeyron latent heat vanishes, has 3D Ising exponents (β≈0.326, γ≈1.237). Critical opalescence is the visible sign of the diverging compressibility.

name: Lattice-gas isomorphism: fluids and magnets
summary: The substitution n_i=(1+s_i)/2 maps a lattice gas exactly onto the Ising model, with chemical potential corresponding to field and coexistence to h=0. This is why liquid–gas, binary-alloy and uniaxial-magnet critical points share exponents.

name: Van der Waals and Maxwell construction as mean field
summary: The van der Waals equation is the mean-field (Landau) theory of the liquid–gas transition, and it is exact in the Kac long-range limit (Lebowitz–Penrose). The Maxwell construction resolves its loop, and it predicts β=1/2 and δ=3; real fluids instead show 3D Ising exponents (β≈0.326).
breaks: Real fluids have 3D Ising exponents (β≈0.326), not mean-field ones; van der Waals neglects the fluctuations that dominate below d=4.

name: Weak localization as a failure of Boltzmann transport
summary: Boltzmann (Drude) transport adds scattering probabilities and so ignores interference. Coherent backscattering along time-reversed paths gives the weak-localization correction, logarithmic in 2D, and the Boltzmann description fails completely at the Ioffe–Regel limit k_F l ~ 1.

name: One-parameter scaling theory of localization
summary: The 'gang of four' recast Anderson localization as an RG flow of the dimensionless conductance g with system size. In the orthogonal class β(g)<0 for all g in d≤2, so there is no metal; the symplectic (spin–orbit) class does allow a 2D metal. In d=3 an unstable fixed point g_c is the mobility edge, a critical point with ν≈1.57 (orthogonal).

name: Mermin–Wagner and the limits of 2D order
summary: The Mermin–Wagner theorem, a statement about thermal fluctuations of Goldstone modes in equilibrium ensembles, forbids continuous-symmetry long-range order at T>0 in d≤2. Its Bose-gas counterpart (Hohenberg) forbids a condensate in interacting 2D gases. Both leave room for BKT quasi-long-range order with power-law correlations.

name: Onsager transfer-matrix solution of 2D Ising
summary: Onsager solved the 2D Ising model with the transfer-matrix method: Z=Tr T^N reduces to the largest eigenvalue, which gives T_c and the logarithmic specific heat. The exponent β=1/8 required a separate calculation of the spontaneous magnetization (announced by Onsager in 1949, derived by Yang in 1952).

name: Toric-code threshold as a random-bond Ising transition
summary: Optimal decoding of the surface code under independent bit-flip noise maps onto the 2D random-bond Ising model on the Nishimori line. The error threshold p_c≈10.9% is that model's ordering transition, and spin-glass replica tools now analyze qLDPC codes.

name: Blackbody radiation shift in optical clocks
summary: The ambient Planck radiation field Stark-shifts clock transitions by an amount ∝T⁴, with a small dynamic correction ∝T⁶. It is a leading systematic of optical lattice clocks, and controlling it has driven cryogenic clocks and in-situ thermometry at the 10^-18 to 10^-19 level.

name: Bose–Einstein condensation from quantum statistics to atoms
summary: The BEC transition predicted by Bose–Einstein counting, nλ³=ζ(3/2), was realized in 1995 in dilute alkali gases. Harmonic traps change the density of states (k_BT_c≈0.94ħω̄N^{1/3}), and interactions and finite size shift T_c by a few percent, a shift that has been measured.
breaks: Ideal-gas T_c is exact only for non-interacting bosons. Weak interactions shift it and change the critical behaviour to the 3D XY class.

name: Thermal noise and cooling of mechanical oscillators
summary: A mechanical resonator's thermal force noise follows from the FDT applied to its susceptibility, and cavity sideband cooling engineers a colder effective bath. The Stokes/anti-Stokes asymmetry (∝ n̄+1 vs n̄) reflects quantum zero-point fluctuations, including detector noise, and serves as a primary thermometer.

name: Caldeira–Leggett: quantum Brownian motion
summary: A particle linearly coupled to an Ohmic bath of oscillators obeys the classical Langevin equation at high T, but in quantum form it decoheres spatial superpositions at a rate ∝ γ(Δx/λ_th)². Classical friction and quantum decoherence come from one bath spectral density.
breaks: The rate formula assumes an ohmic, Markovian bath at high temperature. At low T the dynamics is non-Markovian and zero-point bath fluctuations change the rate.

name: Kibble–Zurek measurement of BEC critical exponents
summary: Quenching a homogeneous Bose gas through T_c freezes in coherence domains whose size scales as τ_Q^{ν/(1+zν)}. Navon et al. (2015) measured this exponent as ≈0.35, giving z≈1.4 given ν≈0.67. Earlier, correlation-length measurements in a trapped gas found ν≈0.67, consistent with 3D XY (Donner 2007).

name: Gross–Pitaevskii and BCS–BEC crossover as mean field
summary: The Gross–Pitaevskii equation is the Hartree mean-field theory of a condensate, with the macroscopic wavefunction as the Landau order parameter; its stationary form is a Ginzburg–Landau equation. For fermions, Eagles–Leggett BCS mean field with a self-consistent chemical potential interpolates from BCS pairs to molecular BEC across a Feshbach resonance.
breaks: GP is a T=0 dynamical equation, not a free energy near T_c, and fails in strongly fluctuating 1D gases. Beyond-mean-field (Lee–Huang–Yang) terms matter at higher density, and crossover mean field is only qualitative at unitarity.

name: BKT transition in 2D atomic gases
summary: Quasi-2D trapped Bose gases show the BKT transition directly: interference contrast reveals quasi-long-range phase coherence below T_BKT, and free vortices proliferate above it. Uniform-box gases later confirmed the universal superfluid-density jump.

name: Black-hole mechanics as thermodynamics
summary: Stationary black holes obey the zeroth, first and second laws with κ as temperature and A/4 as entropy. Hawking radiation makes this physical: T_H = ħκ/2πck_B. Bekenstein's generalized second law extends the second law; C = −8πGM²k_B/ħc < 0. The third law holds only in unattainability form, since extremal holes have T=0, S≠0.
map: dM=\frac{\kappa}{8\pi G}dA+\Omega_HdJ+\Phi_HdQ\leftrightarrow dU=TdS+\cdots;\ \delta(S_{\rm out}+S_{BH})\ge0;\ C=-\frac{8\pi GM^2k_B}{\hbar c}

name: Euclidean gravity partition function
summary: Gibbons and Hawking computed black-hole thermodynamics from a canonical partition function: the Euclidean action of the black hole, smooth only if imaginary time has period ħ/k_BT_H, gives F=-k_BT ln Z and the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy. Negative heat capacity makes the flat-space canonical ensemble unstable unless the system is boxed (York) or in AdS.
map: Z=\int\mathcal Dg\,e^{-I_E[g]/\hbar}\approx e^{-I_E^{\text{cl}}},\ I_E=\beta M/2\Rightarrow S=\beta M-I_E=A/4G

name: Microcanonical counting of black-hole microstates
summary: Strominger and Vafa counted the D-brane bound states carrying the charges of a 5D extremal BPS black hole, using Cardy's asymptotic density of states of the dual 2D CFT. The microcanonical S = ln Ω matches A/4G at leading order in large charges.

name: Hawking radiation is a Planck spectrum
summary: Bogoliubov mixing of in- and out-modes at a horizon gives exactly Bose–Einstein (Fermi–Dirac for fermions) occupation at T_H, filtered by greybody factors. The mass-loss rate is roughly Stefan–Boltzmann for an emitter of area ~27πM², corrected by greybody factors and the number of light species.

name: Hawking–Page transition and deconfinement
summary: In global AdS, thermal radiation and large black holes exchange dominance in a first-order Hawking–Page transition at T~1/ℓ_AdS. Via AdS/CFT this is a large-N deconfinement transition of the dual gauge theory on S³ (Witten), with free energy jumping from O(1) to O(N²) and the Polyakov loop as order parameter.
map: I_{BH}-I_{\rm AdS}\propto r_+^{d-1}(\ell^2-r_+^2)\ \text{in AdS}_{d+1},\ \text{sign change at}\ r_+=\ell

name: Choptuik critical collapse: universality and scaling
summary: At the threshold of black-hole formation, the final mass scales as M∝(p-p*)^γ with γ≈0.37 independent of the initial-data family. The critical solution is a self-similar attractor with a single unstable mode, so γ=1/λ like ν=1/y_t at an RG fixed point.
breaks: There is no thermal ensemble or fluctuation-driven criticality: it is deterministic PDE dynamics near a codimension-one fixed point, and the 'universality class' depends on the matter model (γ differs for radiation fluids).

name: Directed percolation is Reggeon field theory
summary: The field theory of directed percolation is identical to Reggeon field theory, developed in the 1970s for high-energy hadron scattering. Its ε-expansion around d_c=4 transferred directly to absorbing-state transitions.

name: WIMP freeze-out from the Boltzmann equation
summary: Relic dark-matter abundance comes from a Boltzmann equation in an expanding universe. Annihilation keeps n near equilibrium until the rate n⟨σv⟩ falls below H, after which the comoving density freezes out at Ω h²∝1/⟨σv⟩.

name: Electroweak crossover at T ~ 160 GeV
summary: Electroweak symmetry is restored at high temperature. Dimensional reduction to a 3D SU(2)-Higgs theory and lattice simulations show that for m_h=125 GeV the transition is a smooth crossover, beyond the endpoint (in the 3D Ising class) of the first-order line. Standard-Model electroweak baryogenesis is therefore ruled out.

name: Pisarski–Wilczek: universality of the chiral transition
summary: Pisarski and Wilczek used symmetry and the ε-expansion to argue that the chiral transition with two massless flavours is in the 3D O(4) class (if the U(1)_A anomaly stays strong), while with three massless flavours it is first order (no infrared-stable fixed point). Physical quark masses give a crossover at T_pc ≈ 156 MeV.
map: SU(2)_L\times SU(2)_R\simeq O(4)\Rightarrow\text{3D }O(4)\ \text{class};\ N_f=3:\ \text{cubic invariant}\Rightarrow\text{first order}
breaks: Lattice studies (Cuteri, Philipsen and Sciarra 2021) suggest a second-order chiral limit even for N_f=3. The size of U(1)_A breaking at T_c remains debated.

name: NJL: BCS mean field for chiral symmetry breaking
summary: Nambu and Jona-Lasinio modelled nucleon mass generation explicitly on the BCS gap equation. The constituent mass is a self-consistent mean field from a four-fermion attraction, with pions as Goldstone modes, and the NJL model remains a mean-field tool for QCD phase diagrams.

name: Reactors as heat sources for Rankine cycles
summary: Fission reactors and fusion plants are heat sources whose electrical efficiency (~33% for LWRs, more for high-temperature designs) is bounded by Carnot at the coolant outlet temperature and achieved with Rankine or Brayton cycles. Decay heat after shutdown is a thermodynamic safety problem.

name: Nuclear liquid–gas transition and the QCD phase diagram
summary: Nuclear matter has a liquid–gas first-order line ending in a critical point (T_c≈15–20 MeV near saturation density). A conjectured QCD critical endpoint at high μ_B would share its Ising (Z₂) universality class. Both are analysed with Gibbs coexistence in (T, μ_B).
breaks: The QCD endpoint is conjectured, not observed. Its Z₂ is emergent from chiral/deconfinement dynamics, while the liquid–gas transition comes from nucleon interactions; finite nuclei blur the nuclear one.

name: Nuclear statistical equilibrium and the deuterium bottleneck
summary: Early-universe abundances follow the Saha/law-of-mass-action equation μ_A=Zμ_p+Nμ_n. Deuterium is suppressed until T≈0.07 MeV, well below its 2.2 MeV binding energy, because the photon-to-baryon ratio η⁻¹~10⁹ is huge (entropy wins).

name: Liquid-drop model: nuclei as droplets of nuclear liquid
summary: The semi-empirical mass formula is the leptodermous (volume plus surface) expansion of a droplet of saturated, incompressible liquid. The volume term is the bulk chemical potential, and the surface term is a surface tension σ≈1 MeV/fm², the same capillarity that sets nucleation barriers.
map: B=a_VA-a_SA^{2/3}-\cdots\ \leftrightarrow\ G=-\Delta\mu N+4\pi r^2\sigma,\ a_S=4\pi r_0^2\sigma
breaks: Nuclei have only ~10–300 constituents, so curvature and shell corrections (magic numbers) are comparable to surface terms. The 'liquid' is a quantum Fermi liquid with pairing, not a classical van der Waals fluid.

name: Statistical hadronization and the thermal model
summary: Hadron yields across species and collision energies follow a grand-canonical hadron-resonance-gas partition function with just T_ch≈156 MeV and μ_B(√s), which coincides with the lattice crossover. In small systems strangeness is suppressed because exact canonical conservation, not grand-canonical averaging, applies (ensemble inequivalence).

name: Compound-nucleus decay as microcanonical evaporation
summary: Bohr's compound nucleus 'forgets' how it formed and decays statistically. Weisskopf evaporation and Hauser–Feshbach theory compute decay widths from detailed balance and level densities, so emission spectra are Maxwellian with a nuclear temperature T=(∂ln ρ/∂E)^{-1}. This is microcanonical statistical mechanics of a ~100-body system.

name: Stefan–Boltzmann limit of the quark–gluon gas
summary: An ideal QGP is a relativistic Bose (gluons) plus Fermi (quarks) gas, ε/T⁴=(π²/30)(16+(21/2)n_f), and the jump from ~3 pion degrees of freedom to ~47.5 signals deconfinement. Lattice pressure reaches ~80% of this at a few T_c, a deficit that resummed (HTL) perturbation theory largely reproduces.

name: Neutron degeneracy pressure and β-equilibrium
summary: Neutron-star matter is a degenerate Fermi system. Oppenheimer and Volkoff found that an ideal neutron Fermi gas supports at most ~0.7 M_⊙, and the observed 2 M_⊙ stars require repulsive interactions. Equilibrium composition follows from μ_n=μ_p+μ_e at T≈0.

name: Fermi-gas nuclear level densities
summary: Bethe's level-density formula treats the nucleus as a degenerate Fermi gas. The Sommerfeld expansion gives E*=aT² and S=2aT, so ρ(E)∝exp(2√(aE)) with a≈A/8 MeV⁻¹. These level densities feed Hauser–Feshbach rates for reactors and the r-process.

name: Neutron–proton freeze-out as rate competition
summary: The n/p ratio tracks its equilibrium value e^{-Q/T} until weak rates Γ∝G_F²T⁵ fall below the Hubble rate H∝T²/M_Pl at T_f≈0.8 MeV, freezing n/p≈1/6. Neutron decay until the deuterium bottleneck breaks lowers it to ≈1/7, giving Y_p≈2(n/p)/(1+n/p)≈0.25.
